claims.quote: But that semi-elected, semi-nominated body of a few score of persons of both sexes, controls this planet.
claims.description: A small world body, the Aerial Board of Control, effectively governs the whole planet and confirms or annuls international arrangements.

claims.quote: Here she will stay a shutterless observatory; a life-boat station; a salvage tug; a court of ultimate appeal-cum-meteorological bureau for three hundred miles in all directions, till Wednesday next when her relief slides across the stars to take her buffeted place.
claims.description: Airborne Mark Boats hover in fixed stations as observatory, rescue and salvage craft and weather bureau for a surrounding region.

claims.quote: A postal packet's dip-dial records every yard of every run.
claims.description: Airborne mail packets carry instruments that automatically record their complete flight path for later analysis.

claims.quote: So far, we can drag out the dawn to twice its normal length in these latitudes. But some day—even on the Equator—we shall hold the Sun level in his full stride.
claims.description: Aircraft fly fast enough westward to stretch the dawn, with a dream of eventually keeping pace with the Sun even at the equator.

claims.quote: We hoist 'em in sterilized air for a while.
claims.description: Airborne hospital ships carry tuberculosis patients up into sterilized high-altitude air as treatment.

claims.quote: How much do the doctors say we've added to the average life of man?
claims.description: Medical progress has substantially increased average human lifespan (answered as thirty years).

claims.quote: Trans-Asiatic Directs we met, soberly ringing the world round the Fiftieth Meridian at an honest seventy knots
claims.description: Regular scheduled airships circle the globe on fixed routes at about seventy knots.

claims.quote: And minute by minute our silent clock gives us a sixteen-second mile.
claims.description: Passenger and mail airships cruise at about 225 miles per hour.

claims.quote: The deep-sea freighters are rising to lung up after the long night
claims.description: Large cargo submarines cross the oceans and surface periodically to renew their air.

claims.quote: these heavy freighters fly down to Halifax direct, and scent the air as they go.
claims.description: Heavy bulk cargo such as ore and petroleum is carried by air freighters.

claims.quote: The A. B. C. have taken over the administration of Crete on normal lines
claims.description: Communities give up local self-government and are administered by the world board, with Crete the last holdout of autonomous institutions.

claims.quote: We have been treated to the spectacle of what are practically keeled racing-planes driven a clear five foot or more above the water
claims.description: Racing planes and winged 'bat' boats skim above the water as a competitive sport.

claims.quote: It was curious to watch the action of the holding-down clips all along the frosty river front as the boats cleared or came to rest.
claims.description: Airship landing towers use mechanical clips and arms to receive and hold air vessels.
